gen-gf-unkempt-plus-jakarta-sans: Expressive from the first letter, Unkempt gives its t a crossbar as hefty as the stem, while Plus Jakarta Sans stays precise. Its monoline curves stop well short of closing up.
gen-gf-unkempt-sora: Sora is precise and geometric, its curves turning corners with no pressure swell at all. But Unkempt does its best commanding a room, while Sora does its best staying precise.
gen-gf-unkempt-space-grotesk: A t whose crossbar matches its stem in weight marks Unkempt. Space Grotesk, drawn as one constant ribbon of width, gives paragraphs open counters that breathe all the way down the column.
gen-gf-warnes-fs-merriweather-sans: Expressive and stretched out, Warnes draws every stroke at a single thickness and lets the ink taper off before it touches. Merriweather Sans brings sturdy, tall-standing lowercase, its e opening clearly to the right.
gen-irish-grover-fs-merriweather-sans: Words in the body look sturdy and large, a steady partner for the fun, organic heading in Irish Grover. Merriweather Sans would hold up across pages of text, its e opening clearly to the right.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-asap: Autour One draws bold, round letters with a stroke like a stylus held at fixed pressure. And Asap does the readable work, with open arcs for its c and a body height close to the capitals.
gen-audiowide-satoshi: Futuristic from the first glyph, Audiowide sets its letters like tiles with wide grout, while Satoshi opens up beneath it. Satoshi's soaring x-height, cut to one width, feels approachable.
gen-flavors-work-sans: Work Sans reads modern, with c tips that never creep toward touching. Flavors handles the commanding whimsy with its towering x-height, while Work Sans handles the quiet, contemporary reading.
gen-gf-goldman-switzer: Wide-set and loud: Goldman gives its round forms, which read like open parentheses, generous clearance. And Switzer's wire-like Swiss letters hold every stroke ending at one thickness, giving the loud heading a tidy partner.
gen-eater-fs-quicksand: Eater is dark and aggressive, with wide letter gaps and thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems. But Quicksand draws every bar at one gauge, and that stark gap is what makes the pair work.
